The insurer is in appeal questioning the saddling of the entire liability and also on quantum of compensation,
whereas, the claimants are in appeal, not C/W MFA No. 102130 of 2019 , being satisfied with the quantum of compensation and praying for enhancement of compensation.
2.

The wife, children and parents of deceased Maktum Magatakhan, filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation for the death of Maktum Magatakhan,
in a road traffic accident that occurred on 17.06.2017 involving NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-49/R-955 and a motorcycle.

It is stated that, the deceased was aged about 27 years and was The Divisional Controller vs Kumari Tanjeela D/O Maktum Mugatakhan on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80074332/
3 earning Rs.12,000/- per month by doing Masonry work.

sentences.text: The Insurer filed its objection denying the claim petition averments.

The Insurer contended that the rider of the motorcycle i.e. the deceased was not having valid and effective driving licence and was riding the motorcycle at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner by overtaking another moving vehicle, holding handle with one hand and he was using his another hand for cutting Gutka packet by his teeth and he was speaking with the injured-petitioner.
It is the case of the Insurer that the C/W MFA No. 102130 of 2019 , accident took place due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle i.e. deceased.

Before the tribunal, the wife of the deceased/claimant No.1 examined herself as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to P.21 were marked and the respondents examined as R.W.1 i.e. driver of the bus and no documents were marked.

The tribunal on scrutiny of the documents placed on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.14,72,000/- on the following heads :
 Sl.

No . Particulars Amount  1 Towards loss of dependency Rs.13,77,000/-
 2 Towards loss of estate, loss of Rs.70,000/-
 consortium and funeral expenses  3 Towards loss of love and affection Rs.25,000/-
While awarding the above compensation, the tribunal assessed the income at Rs.9,000/- per month, by adopting multiplier '17' and deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased.
Learned counsel Sri. M.K.Soudagar, appearing for NWKRTC would submit that, the accident took place solely due to the negligent driving of the rider of the deceased.

He submits that, the deceased was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and he was cutting Gutka packet from his teeth, while riding the motorcycle which is the root cause for the occurrence of the accident.

In support of the above contention, he submits that, R.W.1 the driver of the bus is examined and the tribunal has committed an error in saddling the entire liability on the NWKRTC without appreciating the material evidence on record.

5. Learned counsel would further submit that, the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal is on the higher side and he prays for reduction in the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal.

6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. G.R.Turamari, appearing for the claimants would submit that the tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the C/W MFA No. 102130 of 2019 ,

Learned counsel would further submit that, the tribunal failed to add 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects which the claimants would be entitle in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Having heard the learned counsels for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the following points would arise for our consideration:
(i) Whether the tribunal is justified in saddling the entire liability on the NWKRTC?
(ii) Whether the claimants would be entitle for enhancement of the compensation?
8. Answer to the above points would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
The accident which took place on 17.06.2017 involving the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-49/R- 2515 and NWKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-49/R- 955 and the resultant death of one Maktum Mugatakhan, is not in dispute in these appeals.
9.
The main contention of the NWKRTC is that, the accident took place totally due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle i.e. the deceased.
Learned counsel would submit that, to support its contention the driver i.e. R.W.1 was examined.

R.W.1 has stated that the deceased C/W MFA No.
102130 of 2019 , was trying to cut Gutka packet by his teeth while riding the motorbike which is the root cause for the accident.
But it is to be noticed that, the wife who was the pillion rider, who examined herself as P.W.1 has denied the said suggestion.
The driver who is an interested witness and his evidence without any corroborative material or evidence cannot be believed.
Therefore, we do not see any reason to interfere with the finding of the tribunal.
10. The income of the deceased assessed by the tribunal at Rs.9,000/- per month is on the lower side.
The claimants have stated that the deceased was earning Rs.22,000/- per month by doing Masonry work, but no material is placed on record to establish the income.
In the absence of material to assess the income it is for the Courts and tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The petitioner income as assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side.

This Court and the Lok Adalaths while settling the accident claims of the year 2017 would normally assess the income at Rs.10,250/-

sentences.text: Taking note of the same, we are inclined to assess the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.10,250/- per month.

The claimants would be entitled for adding 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi, as the deceased was aged 27 years.
Further the deduction of 1/4th towards the personal expenses of the deceased and the multiplier of '17' is proper and correct which needs no interference.

Rs.10,250/- + 40% = Rs.14,350/- minus 1/4th deduction = Rs.10,763/-
Rs.10,763/-X 12 X 17 = Rs.21,95,652/-
11. The Hon'ble Apex Court
in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited (supra), has made it clear that, the claimants would be entitle for spousal, parental and filial consortium.

In the instant case, the dependents are the wife, children and parents of the deceased and therefore, they would be entitle for Rs.40,000/- under the head of spousal, parental and filial - 11 - C/W MFA No. 102130 of 2019 , consortium, apart from Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
12.
